issues.failure_explanation: Membership of the bubble space in the enhanced space of degree k+2 requires (b - Pi^nabla_{k+2} b, q) = 0 for all monomials q of degrees k+1 and k+2. A bubble b in B_{k+2\k} has vanishing moments only up to degree k-2; its moments of degrees k+1 and k+2 are generically nonzero and are not reproduced by Pi^nabla_{k+2} b, so these orthogonality conditions fail (for k=1 on a square, bubble{3} is 3-dimensional while the 7 conditions (b - Pi^nabla_3 b, q) = 0 with q in monomials_3 \ monomials_1 are generically independent). Hence V_k(K) is not contained in [enhanced{k+2}(K)]^2; only the weaker inclusion in the enlarged (plain) space [enlarged{k+2}(K)]^2 holds. The proposition the claim was meant to justify (unisolvence of dofs(v), prop:added-4) is nevertheless true by a direct argument: zero dofs(v) force tilde = 0 by unisolvence of the enhanced degrees of freedom (the bubble vanishes on the boundary and is orthogonal to P_{k-2}), and then bolla_h = 0 because its moments of degrees k-1 and k vanish.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the false inclusion by the true statement V_k(K) subset [enlarged{k+2}(K)]^2 (or delete it) and prove prop:added-4 directly from the direct-sum decomposition V_k(K) = [enhanced{k}]^2 + [B_{k+2\k}]^2, noting that dofs(v) are exactly the unisolvent degrees of freedom of the enhanced part plus the moments of degrees k-1 and k that determine the bubble.
issues.overall_effect: The stated justification for the unisolvence of the velocity degrees of freedom is invalid as written; the unisolvence proposition itself (prop:added-4) survives through a direct argument that the source does not provide.
issues.title: False claim that the MINI-VEM velocity space is contained in the enhanced VEM space of degree k+2, used to justify unisolvence of the velocity degrees of freedom
issues.why_classification: The false claim is isolated and the proposition it supports is independently true; the repair is a one-line replacement of the justification with no loss of any result, rate, or guarantee.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof takes v(q_h) in V = [H^1_0]^2 from the surjectivity of the divergence and forms its VEM interpolant v_I. The source defines the interpolant only for w in H^1(K) intersect C^0(K); an H^1 function in two dimensions need not be continuous, and its vertex and edge point values (the degrees of freedom of the enhanced space) are not defined, so v_I is not well-defined by the stated definition. In addition, the test function actually built, v_h = v_I + bolla_h, is never rescaled to satisfy the required normalization ||v_h||_{1,Omega} = ||q_h||_{0,Omega} (the rescaling is omitted), and the stability bound ||v_I||_1 <= C||v(q_h)||_1 used later presupposes a well-defined, stable interpolant.

issues.failure_explanation: The formulation (Problem pro:stokes and the discrete space V_k subset [H^1_0]^2) imposes homogeneous Dirichlet boundary conditions. In Test 2, u_1(x,1) = x^2(x-1)^2 is nonzero on the top edge. The source describes no lifting of the boundary data, so the discrete solution u_h in [H^1_0]^2 cannot converge to u in H^1: liminf ||u - u_h||_{1,Omega} is bounded below by the H^1 norm of any lifting of the boundary trace, which is positive, hence the O(h^k) H^1 rate cannot hold for Test 2 as described. The claim that the estimates of Section 9 'are confirmed by all the numerical tests' is therefore unsupported as written: either a lifting was used and must be described, or the Test 2 convergence results are invalid.

failure_location.quote: The velocity in Test~1 has homogeneous Dirichlet boundary conditions on the entire $\partial\Omega$, whereas the velocity in Test~2 has nonzero Dirichlet boundary conditions on the top edge of the domain.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Describe the standard lifting in the numerical section: write u = g~ + u~ with g~ a computable lifting of the top-edge trace and u~ in [H^1_0]^2, solve the discrete problem with right-hand side f + Delta g~ (projected as usual), and measure the errors against u~ (equivalently u - g~). If no lifting was in fact used, the Test 2 experiments must be redone with one.
issues.overall_effect: The numerical confirmation claimed for Test 2 (all polynomial degrees and all four mesh families) is unreliable as described; the theoretical estimates and the Test 1 results are unaffected.
issues.title: Test 2 has nonzero Dirichlet boundary data but no lifting is described, so the claimed confirmation of the error estimates for all numerical tests is unsupported
issues.why_classification: A standard lifting repair is short and routine and preserves every reported rate; the defect is an omission in the description of the tests, not in the method or the theory.
